entries.note: “Might” explicitly frames the plateau as a possibility.

entries.test: Public benchmark results and independent comparisons available by March 16, 2024 would show whether any competing model decisively exceeded GPT-4 across capabilities.
entries.note: The absence of a decisive competitor is asserted firmly; convergence is tentative.

entries.test: Public application demonstrations, product launches and deployment reports from GPT-4's first year would establish the extent of progress in applications and practical use.
entries.note: The birthday context supports the past-year horizon.

entries.test: Representative adoption surveys and engineering reports available at publication would show production difficulties and whether most LLM deployment efforts remained preliminary.
entries.note: “Preliminary” has a plain reading here as experimentation or pilots preceding production.

entries.test: Company statements and adoption surveys through publication, compared with earlier expectations and actual results, would show whether companies were lowering expectations and whether many initial expectations exceeded demonstrated capabilities.
entries.note: The claim concerns observable corporate expectations and results.

entries.test: Public incident reports, threat intelligence and documented influence operations would establish whether bad actors had used LLMs for cybercrime and disinformation by publication.
entries.note: “Appear” qualifies the evidence for existing activity rather than predicting a possible future use.

entries.test: Reproducible evaluations of GPT-4-class models available at publication would show whether hallucinations, instability and occasional nonsensical errors persisted.
entries.note: “Unsolved” is faithful when read as persisting, rather than impossible to solve.

entries.test: Public comparisons of competing models' capabilities, costs and availability through publication would show whether multiple competitors were closing OpenAI's lead.
entries.note: The surrounding capability comparison gives “moat” a concrete competitive reading.

entries.test: Public pricing histories and provider announcements would show successive competitive price cuts among LLM providers.
entries.note: “We can expect” expresses a firm expectation without a deadline.

entries.test: Public court proceedings, judgments, settlements and company disclosures would show whether disputes over training sources became a substantial legal and business issue for the industry.
entries.note: The reference to sources supports the training-data interpretation; no deadline is stated.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and credible reporting on LLM revenues, operating costs and margins at publication would show whether sustainable profitability had been established.
entries.note: This describes the unresolved commercial position at publication, rather than predicting inevitable losses.
“Far more” adds a comparative magnitude absent from the source. The passage combines current high costs with explicitly possible additional costs, rather than a firm forecast.
